problem.text: Mike cycled $15$ laps in $57$ minutes. Assume he cycled at a constant speed throughout. Approximately how many laps did he complete in the first $27$ minutes?

steps.title: Where to start: constant speed means proportional
steps.body: The clue is "constant speed". It means laps and time grow together: in a certain fraction of the time, Mike rides the same fraction of the laps. So first find what fraction of the $57$ minutes the first $27$ minutes are.

steps.title: Find the time for one lap
steps.body: Another way to see the rate: $15$ laps in $57$ minutes means each lap takes $$\frac{57}{15} = 3.8 \text{ minutes}.$$ Careful: do not round $3.8$ down to $3$. That is almost a whole minute per lap, and over $27$ minutes the error adds up to about two laps.

your_turn.prompt: How long do $5$ laps take at this pace?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The number of laps is $15\cdot\frac{9}{19} = \frac{135}{19} \approx 7.1$. Check: $7$ laps take $7 \times 3.8 = 26.6$ minutes, just under $27$. Also, $\frac{27}{57}$ is a bit less than $\frac12$, so the answer should be a bit less than half of $15$, which is $7.5$. The answer is **(B)** $7$.

wrong_choices.C: This comes from rounding $3.8$ minutes per lap down to $3$, which gives $27 \div 3 = 9$. Check it: $9$ laps at $3.8$ minutes each take over $34$ minutes, far more than $27$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
